author_sources.rule: xprime=u.r join x.l; yprime=x.r join y.l
a(xprime)=a(x) when xprime.r=x.l; b(xprime)=b(u) when xprime.l=u.r

T: swap a,b bits; names and edges unchanged
tau: same names and edges; a_i <- a_(i+1), b_i <- b_(i-1)

P_raw.edges: for all u,x,y in old V: (R(u) join L(x)):b -> (R(y) join L(u)):a; no printed adjacency guards
P_raw.bits: printed LHS a_i(x),b_i(x) uses unbound x rather than quantified xprime
P_raw.evaluation: evaluate structural formula in both engines; do not invent bit assignment or inverse for an incomplete specification

P_ring.role: explicit historical ring completion for executable control, not a silently repaired P_raw
completions: restrict triples to consecutive y,u,x on the old directed ring
replace unbound bit destination x by xprime
P_ring.inverse: for edge u:b -> v:a: z=R(v) join L(u), a(z)=a(u), b(z)=b(v); reverse midpoint incidence

A.role: ring normalization of both author clarifications
A.inverse: same midpoint names and incidence as Q_A; a from u_i,b from u_(i+1)

I.split: (u,3) -> (L(u),1),(R(u),2) with old a attached left, old b attached right

G1_A1_method: Finite name terms decompose into atomic binary-prefix cylinders. Pairwise prefix overlap (including inside one name) is exactly a shared descendant; reject it. Ordered-ring engine uses pairwise comparison; explicit graph engine uses tries.
scope: main initial simple cycles L3..6; small 1/2 vertex port cycles explicitly separated and allowed as outputs; reachable finite canonical terms; no arbitrary graph/topology or theorem attestation
independence: ring engine: tuple terms, index scan, cyclic sequence; graph engine: string terms, incidence maps, simultaneous boundary rewrites; neither imports the other; direct tau oracle imports neither transition rule
